correctness.rationale: Lipparini established strong amalgamation/Fraisse limit and ultrahomogeneity for the exact two-reflexive-partial-order language with relation inclusion. Coordinate labeling of injective tuples gives P⊆Q on [n], any such pair embeds by universality, and equal labeled restrictions imply an automorphism by ultrahomogeneity; differing restrictions cannot belong to the same orbit. For noninjective tuples the equality-kernel partition has k blocks and a labeled injective orbit, proving b_n=Σ_{k=0}^n S(n,k)a_k. Independent Python transitivity-oriented enumeration of all labeled posets P⊆Q reproduces 1,5,79,3221,301831 through n=5, using direct pair-subset tests unrelated to the zeta implementation. Bundled verify.cpp and output inspected; it states an exhaustive n=6 3^15-zeta computation recovering 60,305,525; that specific n=6 value was not independently executed here, so independently established finite coverage stops at n=5. The formula for all n has a separate conceptual proof.
